title: Units regulators and hR validation
objective: Implement rigorous outward Arb enclosure transport, precision-safe regulator refinement, bounded exact unit p-saturation, and adaptive analytic retry hooks

exceptions: The existing FLINT Node-API host adapter must export exact Arb dyadic endpoints; ordinary Python consumes that proof boundary and fails closed when the native capability is absent.

handoff.summary: Added a hash-bound UnitSaturationIndexCertificate that binds the maximal-order identity, initial units, class number, complete canonical torsion, analytic hR reconstruction, factor-base/relation-generation evidence, and conditional or unconditional proof status. Exact p-saturation now accepts only that replayable certificate as completion authority; bare integers and HRIndexValidationResult objects remain diagnostic. Replay independently recomputes canonical roots of unity and the analytic proof, invokes the external generation-evidence verifier, strictly decodes every authenticated integer/boolean leaf, reconstructs canonical evidence before comparison, and rejects reauthenticated semantic mutations. Target classes are streamed after checked target/candidate/local-work preflight caps with cancellation polling. RationalEndpoint and native dyadic transport reject booleans, floats, and noncanonical decimal integers. The real Q(sqrt(5)) context covers exact index-two enlargement, local obstruction, adaptive retry, conditional propagation, torsion mutation, hash-preserving proof mutations, noncanonical scalar mutations, and large-prime preflight.
risks: Rigorous zeta status assumes the caller supplies the actual maximal-order discriminant and a complete exact splitting provider; the function validates prime coverage and every local degree identity but does not independently prove the field/order identity.

The p-th-root producer is intentionally bounded by an order-coordinate box and candidate cap. Missing roots outside that box never certify saturation; completion then requires exhaustive finite-quotient obstructions for every exponent/torsion target or exhaustion of a rigorously supplied global index.

Only algebraic logarithm inputs cross the corrected Arb endpoint boundary. Determinant and zeta transcendental evaluation remain explicitly typed exact-rational intervals with mpmath.libmp directed rounding, not Arb balls.

FactoredNumberFieldElement currently exposes only scalar qqbarLogAbsBall calls. The measured strict-Python regulator determinant is already sub-millisecond for the rank-two fixture, while zeta finite-interval evaluation dominated the profile, so this lane did not add an unmeasured algebraic-log batch boundary.

A serialized index certificate deliberately needs an application-supplied generation_verifier; its canonical evidence/hash is not treated as self-authenticating. Missing or rejected generation evidence fails closed.

The bounded producer can prove negative p-saturation only when every exponent/torsion target has an exact finite-quotient obstruction. Otherwise it returns incomplete even after exhausting its coordinate box.

The focused Q(sqrt(5)) runtime test took 138.7 seconds for two analytic index constructions plus one independent serialized replay; exact splitting and zeta reconstruction dominate. In-process certificates retain only their explicit field-scoped zeta workspace, while serialized replay intentionally starts independently.

The corrected C source passes a direct syntax check against FLINT headers. This lane's final context receipt borrowed the reconciled linux-x64 addon from the engine-completion worktree because central builds were concurrently replacing their artifacts; broad native/platform gates remain with central integration.
next_steps: Wire certify_unit_saturation_index and ExactUnitSaturationResult into the class/unit engine, passing the full factor-base/relation proof payload and verifier; retain the canonical global_index_certificate in map proofs and call verify_saturation_record on replay.
Run the broad native and platform gates in central integration; no full Arb determinant or zeta migration is claimed by this lane.
